question: E7: does an LSTM fed several rain products side by side (the rain table, the NLDAS rain of the issue day, the ERA5 rain to midnight and the AORC rain to midnight, an analysis made after the fact) warn of more flood onsets 1 day ahead than the LSTM fed the best single product (lstm_wqa, the AORC rain to midnight beside the rain table)?
status: REVIEWED: independent review done (independent AI reviewer agent (Claude), 2026-10-30): verdict 'numbers hold with wording fixes', 2 must-fix, 4 should-fix and 6 notes; 0 numerical mismatches in 8979 values recomputed from results/preds with its own code (results/review_multi_product.json). outcome: Given the NLDAS rain of the issue day, the ERA5 rain to midnight and the AORC rain to midnight (all three made after the fact: NLDAS a gauge analysis published days late, ERA5 a reanalysis, AORC an analysis made after the fact) side by side, beside the rain table, as inputs of the LSTM with the river gauge, onsets warned 1 day ahead go from 52% with the AORC rain to midnight alone (hindsight at most about 4 points) to 56% (single trainings 51% to 58%; the onsets of one storm are not independent): +4.6 points (344 against 316 hits of 611); with the NLDAS and ERA5 columns shuffled within basin, calendar month and split part (the capacity control) 52%, with them one day older (the clock control) 51%; the share of false warnings among the onset warnings is 54% against 51% (754 onset warnings against 643: the trigger-1.0 gain is a higher warning level, not better discrimination: at the triggers chosen on the validation years wqME warns of 48.3% against 48.4% (best onset CSI) and of 24.2% against 25.9% (at most 30% false; capacity control 26.4%, clock control 25.7%)); the median NSE goes from 0.76 to 0.73, lower in 11 of 12 basins (p < 0.001; not a clear loss by the seed rule); by the rule fixed in ROADMAP.md before the first training (section E7, 2026-10-30) this is not a clear gain; the verdict of results/flood_analysis.json is NOT YET for the onsets and CAUTION for all high-flow days.
outcome_caveat: The rule, block by block: block 1, the gain, fails (every seed of wqME above every seed of wqa: no; false share not higher: no; Wilcoxon over the basins p = 0.002, n = 10); block 2, the capacity control flat, holds (median single seed 53.4%, within wqa's 48.6% to 55.3%); block 3, the clock control flat, holds (median single seed 52.0%, within that range). At trigger 1.0 (and so measuring the higher warning level as well), per basin wqME warns of more onsets than wqa in 10 of 12 basins and of fewer in 0 (median difference +4.1 points); 36 onsets are warned only by wqME and 8 only by wqa. The difference in onsets warned 1 day ahead lies between +1.3 and +7.6 points when the test water years and the basins are drawn again (4,000 resamples, the recipe of 13_uncertainty.py; above zero in 99% of them); the training seeds are not drawn again: 5 of the 25 pairs of single trainings go the other way. The difference of the median NSE lies between -0.083 and +0.008. Beside the two products without AORC (lstm_wqnh, 32%) wqME warns of +23.9 points more (169 onsets only by wqME, 23 only by wqnh); the rain table alone (lstm_wq) warns of 19%. Two and three days ahead the median NSE of wqME is 0.32 and 0.23 against 0.38 and 0.26 for wqa. At the 30%-false operating point (the trigger chosen on the validation years so that at most 30% of the onset warnings are false: 1.70) wqME warns of 24% with 31% false on the test years, against 26% with 32% false for wqa (trigger 1.55): 1.6 points fewer. The network yardstick (block 4, not part of the verdict): given the same columns, ridge regression moves by +1.3 points and the random forest by +0.7 against their wqa versions, the LSTM by +4.6: the LSTM gains more from the wqME columns than ridge and forest (at trigger 1.0 only). After the fact: none of the three extra rain products is had at midnight of the issue day: NLDAS is published a few days late and is a daily gauge analysis spread over the hours (results/rain_timing.json), ERA5 is a reanalysis (results/rain_to_midnight.json), and AORC is an analysis made after the fact. The hindsight bound of wqa (hindsight at most about 4 points) was measured for AORC alone and does not bound wqME, whose NLDAS and ERA5 columns are after the fact too: wqME is a test of information, not a forecast that could be issued. The shuffled columns of the capacity control move values between the years of the same split part (50% of them to a day before the day they were measured): they carry no timing information by construction and are a capacity control, not a forecast input. Every number of the new sets is a five-seed number; lstm_wqa has five seeds, lstm_wq and lstm_wqn three.

wilcoxon_over_the_basins.zero_method: wilcox (scipy's default): zero differences are dropped before ranking; n_used counts the basins with a non-zero difference
wilcoxon_over_the_basins.method: scipy.stats.wilcoxon defaults (method='auto', scipy 1.17.1: the exact, permutation or normal-approximation null distribution chosen by scipy from n and the zeros and ties)

block_2_capacity_control_flat.rule: the median of the five single-seed onsets-warned values of wqME_shuf lies within the lowest-highest single-seed range of lstm_wqa (if wqME_shuf gains as much as wqME, the gain is capacity, not information)

block_4_network_yardstick.rule: reported, not part of the verdict: if ridge and forest gain as much from the wqME columns (against their wqa versions of script 16) as the LSTM does, the reading is 'the information, not the network' again
block_4_network_yardstick.reading: the LSTM gains more from the wqME columns than ridge and forest
block_4_network_yardstick.stored_partners: base_linreg_wqa and base_rf_wqa of script 16 (results/preds), rescored here; base_linreg_wqME and base_rf_wqME fitted by this script with the same recipe and settings

interpretations_of_the_rule: Block 1, seed rule: 'above' is strict: the lowest single seed of wqME must be greater than the highest single seed of lstm_wqa (the 'above' of scripts 15-22).
Block 1, false share: 'not higher' means the pooled onset false share of the seed-averaged wqME is at most that of the seed-averaged stored lstm_wqa (equal counts as not higher).

Block 1, Wilcoxon: the per-basin onsets warned are each basin's onset POD at trigger 1.0 from the seed-averaged forecasts; a basin without an onset in the test years would have no value and is left out (counted); zero differences are dropped (scipy's default zero_method='wilcox'), so n_used is the number of basins with a non-zero difference; the p is scipy.stats.wilcoxon with its default method='auto' (as paired() and the scripts before), and the normal-approximation and exact p are recorded beside it. p < 0.05 is required as written; the direction is carried by the seed rule of the same block (a significant loss cannot pass it).

Blocks 2 and 3: 'within' is inclusive (lowest <= median <= highest); the median is numpy's median of the single-seed onsets-warned values of the control (five seeds: the third value); the range of lstm_wqa is over all its stored single seeds (five since 30 October 2026).

Block 4: 'as much' is read on onsets warned at lead 1 (seed-averaged LSTM forecasts, the deterministic simple models): ridge and forest gain as much when each one's gain in points is at least the LSTM's gain; the reading is given in words and is not part of the verdict.

The shuffle (capacity control): within each basin, split part (training, validation, test years) and calendar month, ONE permutation of all days of that month in that part is drawn with numpy's default_rng(SHUF_SEED), basin after basin in the order of the study basins, part after part and month after month (no value crosses a split part); day i of the group then reads the NLDAS and the ERA5 value measured on day perm(i) (one permutation shared by the two columns, so their joint distribution is kept). It is built once, before any training: every seed trains on the same shuffled table.
The older control: day t reads the NLDAS and ERA5 values of day t-1; the first day of the record keeps its own value (the _older controls of scripts 10, 15 and 16).

The resampling interval: 13_uncertainty.py's recipe (test water years and basins drawn again with replacement, B = 4,000, seed 20261004, 2.5th-97.5th percentile of the seed-averaged forecasts' statistic; the 'both' design is the interval quoted, 'years' and 'basins' are stored beside it); the Monte-Carlo noise of the interval ends (13's mc_noise) is not computed.

design.what: one LSTM (flood.LSTMNet, hidden 64) for all 12 basins with the river gauge (log1p flow) and the basin properties (flood.STATIC), the settings of results/lstm_all.json chosen there on the validation years; every set differs only in the daily input columns listed; the trainer stops on the mean validation NSE; the test years 2005-2014 are scored once

wqME.what: the rain table + the NLDAS rain + the ERA5 rain to midnight + the AORC rain to midnight, side by side (the treatment)

wqME_shuf.what: as wqME, the NLDAS and ERA5 columns shuffled within basin x calendar month across years (the same column count and distributions, no timing information)

wqME_older.what: as wqME, the NLDAS and ERA5 columns one day older (is any gain from the issue day's hours?)

wqa.what: the rain table + the AORC rain to midnight (E1b): the number to beat

wqn.what: the rain table + the NLDAS rain of the issue day

wqh.what: the rain table + the ERA5 rain to midnight (E1)

wqnh.what: the rain table + the NLDAS rain + the ERA5 rain to midnight (two products, no AORC)

columns.prcp_nldas: mm: the NLDAS basin-mean rain shipped with CAMELS (the 'prcp' column of the nldas forcing files read by camels.load_basin), the column of scripts 10 and 15 (their sets wqn and wqnh); its day ends at about 17:30 local standard time on day t as measured (results/day_windows.json, day_ends.nldas; the reading of 10_rain_timing.py, not proved again here)
columns.rain_to_midnight: mm: the hourly ERA5 rain of data/hourly/era5_<gauge>.json (the value at time T is the rain of the hour ENDING at T, UTC) summed over the local wall-clock day t of the gauge (00:00 to 24:00, summer time included: every hour goes to the day in which it ends; 23 or 25 hours where the clocks change): the column of script 15 (sets wqh, wqnh)
columns.aorc_to_midnight: mm: the hourly AORC basin means of data/aorc (code/fetch_aorc.py; hour-ENDING UTC stamps; an analysis made after the fact) summed over the same local wall-clock day: the column of script 16 (set wqa) and of code/check_reload.py
columns.older: prcp_nldas_older, rain_to_midnight_older: the same two columns one day older: on issue day t the network reads the values of day t-1 (the first day keeps its own value)
columns.shuf: prcp_nldas_shuf, rain_to_midnight_shuf: the same two columns shuffled within basin x calendar month across the years of the same split part, one permutation per basin-part-month group shared by the two columns (inputs.shuffle): the same values and month-by-month distributions per basin and split part, no timing information about any day

inputs.how_to_read: the three rain products as built here, per basin: the data-side checks of both hourly products (two routes, made-up hours), the shuffle record, and the sha256 of every input column (all basins stacked, float64): a later pass stops if its columns differ

shuffle.what: prcp_nldas_shuf, rain_to_midnight_shuf: the same two columns shuffled within basin x calendar month across the years of the same split part, one permutation per basin-part-month group shared by the two columns (inputs.shuffle): the same values and month-by-month distributions per basin and split part, no timing information about any day
shuffle.unit: single days within basin x calendar month x split part (training, validation and test years each shuffled among themselves)
shuffle.built: once, before any training; every training seed of wqME_shuf reads the same shuffled table
shuffle.statement: The shuffle is a capacity control: its two columns keep each basin's month-by-month values and the pairing of the NLDAS and ERA5 value of a day, but carry no timing information about the day they sit on by construction. Shuffling across years inherently places values measured after a day into that day's inputs (from_a_later_day), but only within the same split part: no test-year value enters a training or validation day and no training-year value a test day (from_another_split_part = 0, asserted). Nothing else is moved: every other input of every day is its own, and the NLDAS and ERA5 values are moved only within the same basin, calendar month and split part. The columns are therefore never a forecast input, only a test of whether two more rain-like columns alone raise the score. Changed on 30 October 2026 before the full training (the smoke test had shuffled over the whole record) so that the split parts stay clean.

column_identity_check.what: before any training: stored networks of scripts 16 (lstm_wqa, AORC) and 15 (lstm_wqnh, NLDAS + ERA5) rebuilt from results/models, run on this script's input table and compared with their stored forecasts in results/preds; equal forecasts prove that this script's prcp_nldas, rain_to_midnight and aorc_to_midnight (and the Daymet columns) are the columns those networks were trained on
column_identity_check.tolerance: numpy.allclose rtol 1e-6, atol 1e-8, the same missing days (the tolerance of the reload asserts of scripts 15-22 and code/check_reload.py)

summary_test.how_to_read: test years, seed average of each LSTM set (the simple models as they are), trigger 1.0, per lead; onset and all = warning tables pooled over the basins; the stored sets rescored here

validation_used_for_no_choice.label: USED FOR NO CHOICE. The validation years choose only the warning levels of verdicts and operating_points, which is labelled there.

resampling.how_to_read: statistics.<name>.<set or pair>.l<k>: value = the test years as they are (equal to flood.evaluate, asserted); years / basins / both = the 2.5th-97.5th percentile over the resamples that draw the test water years / the basins / both again with replacement, and share_above_zero; quote 'both' (13_uncertainty.py). Seed-averaged LSTM forecasts; the single seeds are not resampled. onsets_* are shares (0-1), not points.
resampling.recipe: 13_uncertainty.py: the per-basin, per-water-year sums, basins and water years drawn with replacement (a whole water year stays together, so the days of one storm stay together), every statistic recomputed exactly on each resample, percentile interval
resampling.not_done: the Monte-Carlo noise of the interval ends (13_uncertainty.py mc_noise) and intervals at warning levels chosen on the validation years

yardstick.what: ridge regression and the random forest given the three rain products (rule block 4), by the recipe of 02_baselines.py as script 16 runs it for one column; read in e7_rule.block_4_network_yardstick

recipe_check.what: the recipe of script 16 (features.feature_table for wq + the rain features of aorc_to_midnight, one model per basin and lead fitted on the training years, the settings of results/baselines.json for wq), rebuilt here and compared with its stored forecasts (asserted below 1e-9 mm/day)

checks.base_rf_wqa: not run in this pass (no forest is fitted in this pass; an earlier pass's record is carried below when there is one)

causality.what: (1) data side: both hourly products summed into the wall-clock day by two routes that agree, and the made-up-hours test (every hour ending after 24:00 of a cut day changed: no daily value up to the cut moved, the next day did), per basin, on random days and the first days on which the clocks changed (inputs.data_side); the NLDAS day ends before the issue time by the reading of 10_rain_timing.py (not proved again here); (2) engine: flood.fit runs flood._assert_causal on every network before training (a trained network exists only if it passed); (3) end to end: the made-up-values test on one SAVED network per set (first seed): the set's three rain columns (and in a second round every input column and the flow) of all days after a cut day were replaced by random values (0 to 120 per day); no forecast issued on or before the cut day changed (exactly equal, all three leads, all 12 basins) and the forecasts issued after it did; (4) the simple models: features.py's check with the three columns; (5) the shuffled columns of the capacity control move values between the years of the record (inputs.shuffle.statement): they are no forecast input
causality.engine_check: flood._assert_causal at the start of every flood.fit (asserted: a trained network exists only if it passed)

simple_model_features.what: features.py's check on the real tables: every column of the daily table (the rain table, the three rain products, the flow ...) was replaced after day number 5000 of the record; the feature rows up to the cut did not change and the next row did, in every basin

reload_check.what: one trained network per set (the first seed) rebuilt from its .pt file alone (flood.LSTMNet + the saved weights, settings and scalers), run on the same tables, and compared with the forecasts stored by save_preds
reload_check.tolerance: numpy.allclose, rtol 1e-6, atol 1e-8, missing values equal; same machine

integrity.how_to_read: sha256 of every prediction set and network file of this script, as they are when this file is written; made_in_this_pass lists the files this pass wrote; every other file was only read. A later pass compares the hashes of the files it only reads with these and stops if one differs. stored_sets_read: the files of the stored comparison sets as read (never written by this script).

passes.what: training run: every set and simple model from scratch
rescore (--rescore): scores, tables, outcome and figure recomputed from the saved sets, nothing trained

notes: ROADMAP.md's E7 section has changed since the training pass (fixed_before_training: the two sha256 differ): the rule coded here is the one fixed before training; read the change before quoting.

The stored sets lstm_wqa, lstm_wq, lstm_wqn, lstm_wqh, lstm_wqnh and the stored simple models base_linreg_wqa, base_rf_wqa were rescored by this script's code from results/preds (checks_against_stored_results proves the same numbers as their own results files). The stored networks of lstm_wqa and lstm_wqnh named in column_identity_check were run on this script's table to prove the columns; no other stored network was reloaded.
lstm_wq and lstm_wqn are three-seed sets (04_lstm_all.py, 10_rain_timing.py); they are shown, not part of the rule.

Quoting. Any document must quote outcome_full (outcome plus outcome_caveat), never outcome alone; every number is a seed-averaged number unless it says 'single trainings'; the status field says whether the experiment has been reviewed. E7 is not part of the 2 November hand-in (ROADMAP.md).

264 values in this file are null: a number that is not finite (NaN: a share whose denominator is zero, a p-value that is not defined, the load average, which Windows does not have; 31 of them NaN in this pass's own numbers, the others null already in what this pass read back from the earlier pass) or a value that does not exist. A reader must treat null as 'no value'.
